theme_note: Participants jointly sustain the subreddit’s own April Fools fiction: one presents the supposed leak while replies ask for more, thank the source, and treat the invented game as real. This is separate from canvas conduct.

second_order: calling and joining in to build Starbound
theme_note: These passages recruit people or visibly join the shared canvas work. What varies is the form of participation: calls for help, starting or slowly placing pixels, declaring support, routing helpers to Discord, and asking others to assist.

second_order: working out what and how to draw
theme_note: Participants turn a general wish for Starbound representation into templates, colours, outlines, lettering, borders, alternative sizes, additions, collaborations, and updates. The common practice is deciding and sharing the mark’s concrete form; the proposed forms vary.

second_order: making room with neighbours and allies
theme_note: Participants handle limited canvas space by relocating, restoring neighbours’ work, requesting room, proposing or rejecting pacts, defending prior occupancy, negotiating compromise, and reporting outside help. Cooperation and conflict vary, but each passage works out who can occupy which nearby pixels.

second_order: defending, repairing and watching the mark
theme_note: Participants treat the mark as vulnerable work that needs protection: they report attack or encroachment, call defenders, seek repair aid, rebuild, propose a plan to keep it, and warn of damage. What varies is whether they resist, repair, reclaim, monitor, or contemplate how long they can hold it.

second_order: celebrating, taking pride and crediting the work
theme_note: Participants make the canvas effort into a shared accomplishment by announcing completion, expressing pride, thanking makers, negotiating credit, recounting contributions, and accepting that a temporary mark was still worthwhile. Celebration ranges from triumphant success to pleasure in having taken part despite loss.

second_order: explaining r/place and guiding people to the logo
theme_note: Participants bring less-informed members into the activity by explaining the canvas and its rules or by helping them relocate the Starbound work through coordinates, links, and landmarks. The guidance varies between explaining what the event is and showing where this room’s mark can be found.

second_order: keeping r/place posts from swamping the room
theme_note: Participants manage r/place’s spillover into the subreddit by asking posters to slow down and promising a last update. Later codes can extend this practice if informal restraint becomes thread consolidation.
